A dialog.bottom-sheet (or .bottom) is the surface. Use it for additional or secondary content — not the app’s main view — on compact and medium windows. People dismiss it to get back to the page.

Tokens follow the M3 bottom sheet spec. The container is surface-container-low, 28dp top corners, elevation 1. Max width is 640dp. From the small breakpoint the sheet is inset 56dp from the sides. It never covers the top 72dp of the viewport. The drag handle is a 32×4dp bar in a 48dp hit target.

Two variants, same sheet:

  • Modal — showModal(). A scrim sits behind the sheet and the page is inert. Tap the scrim, drag the handle down, or submit a <form method="dialog"> to dismiss.
  • Standard — show(). No scrim; the page stays interactive. Drag the handle down or use a close action to dismiss.

Now playing

Secondary controls for the current track. The page behind this sheet stays usable.

 
<button type="button" onclick="document.getElementById('sheet').showModal()">
  Show modal
</button>

<dialog id="sheet" class="bottom-sheet">
  <h2>Open file</h2>
  <div>…</div>
  <form method="dialog">
    <button type="submit" class="text" value="cancel">Cancel</button>
  </form>
</dialog>

There is no extra class for the modal variant — showModal() vs show() is the split. The handle is painted with ::before. Put a .handle button first if you want a real control in that slot.

Handle

Drag the top 48dp (or the .handle button) down to dismiss. A flick counts. The rest of the sheet scrolls if the body overflows. 

<dialog class="bottom-sheet">
  <button type="button" class="handle" aria-label="Dismiss"></button>
  <h2>Title</h2>
  …
</dialog>

Layout

Compact (below 601px) is full-bleed, flush to the bottom. From the small breakpoint the sheet is at most 640dp wide with 56dp side inset. It always stops 72dp short of the top. On large screens a side sheet or a basic dialog is usually a better fit; the bottom sheet still lays out if you open one.
